findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

The attested command exited with code 1, with no signal or timeout, after 15.5s against a 180s limit. The expected literal appears in full in stdout (not truncated), and stderr is empty. The proof matches the scenario "An unmapped delivery case prevents execution". It builds a disposable Bun distribution with one shipped profile row removed and leaves the project census untouched. It then makes the plain public request `proof observe-bounded-delivery --json --no-input`. Before the failing assertion, these checks pass: exit code 2, status refused, execution-only authority, a recovery message asking to review a complete mapping, no runner report, a retained diagnostic, and no clone preparation. The only failure is the intended missing behavior: the actor-visible refusal does not name the omitted case identity. The refined check that no mapped identity may appear stops a census dump from satisfying the proof. No wrong-reason failure (syntax, import, fixture, configuration, infrastructure) is present.

The 'no proof execution starts' Then is checked indirectly, by confirming that the diagnostic.log text lacks 'preparing an independent committed clone' and that report_path does not exist. If GREEN rewords that log line, or moves runner launch ahead of clone logging, this negative check could pass even though execution started. Add a check that does not depend on log wording, for example asserting that no clone directory or runner artifact exists in the attempt store, or checking a stage field in the refusal record.

The 'installed observer distribution' is a `bun build` bundle written to packages/cli/dist inside the candidate checkout and run from the candidate root. It is not an installed or unpacked package distribution. That is acceptable for this RED. However, the plan's unmapped-case row describes an installed-distribution boundary, so the distribution-lane proof (bounded-observation-distribution.node.ts) should still cover this refusal through the packaged entrypoints.

The attestation environment runs Node v24.3.0, while the observer contract pins Node v24.18.1. This doesn't affect this RED, because the refusal happens before any tool-inventory checks. If GREEN adds a tool-version preflight ahead of the mapping preflight, this proof could start failing for a different reason (a tool refusal). Keep the mapping refusal ahead of tool checks, or run the harness on the pinned toolchain.

The omitted row is always the first profile entry (`cases.shift()`). An implementation that only reports the first case in declaration order would pass. Consider also removing a row from the middle of the profile so the proof shows the actual missing case is named, not just a positional one.
